reason: The cited evidence (E1) concerns laser-cladded CoCrFeNiTix HEA coatings on Q235, not the native oxide film on pre-exposed Q235 steel. It provides no support for the premises about the natural oxide film's passivation, thermal-stress micro-cracking, or Mn diffusion in the native oxide.
premises: Q235 steel naturally forms a thin, heterogeneous native oxide film
This native oxide film provides passivation against chloride attack at room temperature
Elevated temperature induces thermal stresses that cause micro-cracking in the oxide film
Elevated temperature enhances diffusion of alloying elements (e.g., Mn) that can alter film density and composition
Changes in oxide film integrity and composition modify its barrier properties and corrosion rate
